In the six years since his first interview for the Archive, Dick Hyman has maintained a steady pace of quality musical endeavors. He produces the summer jazz concerts at New York City’s 92nd Street Y, performs at numerous jazz festivals, scores film music, and records for the Arbors record label. Mr.
Hyman will receive an honorary degree from Hamilton College in May of 2002.
Part II was conducted in Clearwater Beach, Florida on March 17, 2001, by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.

My name is Monk Rowe and we are in Clearwater Beach. I’m very pleased to have Dick Hyman with me again today. And this is a real pleasure, first of all just to talk to you, but also because you were my first interview.
That was March ’95 in Scottsdale, Arizona.
Yeah. Well I remember it and of course I’ve seen it, you were kind enough to give me a copy that I saw only recently actually.
I know you have not been idle in the last six years.
No. Do you want a recount?
